### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via validateSecurityPosture (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via validateSecurityPosture (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66e56e26863fa555c0ba149dbfb685b0fe727f49` — the merge of head `781bb576e245139e9abaf8dd6cdf8ecd9c4e88f2` into base `ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66e56e26863fa555c0ba149dbfb685b0fe727f49 && git checkout 66e56e26863fa555c0ba149dbfb685b0fe727f49
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd 781bb576e245139e9abaf8dd6cdf8ecd9c4e88f2 && git checkout -B drift-repro ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd && git merge --no-ff 781bb576e245139e9abaf8dd6cdf8ecd9c4e88f2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

1. ADR-0086 status line — RIGHT. The Re-evaluation table's `everyone` / `guest` row (`:444`) reads "Packages *suggest* bindings; admins confirm", as quoted. Suggestions are `everyone`-only in code: `collectDeclaredSuggestions` hard-codes `anchor = EVERYONE_POSITION` (suggested-audience-bindings.ts `:372`) and `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion` refuses any row whose anchor is not `everyone` (`:834`). The link target exists, the date is the ruling's (comment 6159279205, 2026-10-14), the shape is the paragraph's existing inline Amended clause, and the table row itself is untouched (AGENTS.md rule 13).
2. ADR-0090 status line — RIGHT. D9's last bullet (`:377-378`, "a package may suggest bindings to `everyone` **or** `guest`; the admin confirms each individually") is the bullet named, and it is D9's last. "No package suggestion, no confirmation" is the same two code sites. "No operator bind" holds because the `guest` position's definition is sealed: a save of the built-in `guest` position answers 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, the package door refuses a built-in position name, and `sys_position_permission_set` retired with #15204 stage 8 — ADR-0138 D3 item 5 and its Enforcement map row ("enforced"), with the two refusals recorded in the plugin-security and metadata-protocol changelogs; not re-run here. Date 2026-10-14 is the ruling's, which is what the sibling lines do (the line citing 6159300530 carries 2026-10-14, the line citing 6181988435 carries 2026-10-15: each its ruling's date). D9's decision text is untouched.

6. position.zod.ts anchor docblock (`:164-167`) — RIGHT. "Packages SUGGEST bindings to `everyone` at install time and the admin confirms each": the collector and the confirm door above; "install time" is ADR-0090 D5's term for the sync, which runs at boot and on every list read (suggested-audience-bindings.ts `:236`, `:796`), and was the sentence's existing framing. The `guest` sentence is item 5's wording. The retained clause "its bindings face the strictest lint tier" now reads as the tier definition (`describeAnchorForbiddenBits`'s `guest` arm), consistent with the new sentence: no binding exists to face it yet.

Public surface the diff implies: `@objectstack/spec` ships the changed docblock twice. `src/identity/position.zod.ts` is in the tarball by `files[]` (`src/**/*.zod.ts`), and the JSDoc on `EVERYONE_POSITION` / `GUEST_POSITION` is emitted into `dist/*.d.ts` (tsup `dts` is on). That split is what ② turns on.

Sibling text outside the card, for the seat to file, not a verdict item: `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:69-70` says the `everyone` / `guest` anchor bindings "reject high-privilege sets at the data layer for every caller". ### ② Semver level

FAIL item: `skip-changeset` is wrong for this diff, because of `@objectstack/spec`.

- `@objectstack/spec` (`18.0.0-next.2`, not private): the tarball's bytes change in two shipped files (above). AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 defines the label: "for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package". This diff publishes a corrected docblock from a released package — a fix to author-facing published text, which is the card's own class (a trap for an author or an AI), so it is exactly what an upgrading agent greps `CHANGELOG.md` for. The dispatch claim (6205778566) said so in advance: "A changeset only if a published file's text changes (`patch`)." The dev measured that a published file's text changes and then chose the label on os-dev's comment fast-track (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:300`, comments do not publish). That fast-track is a shortcut whose premise os-dev's own criterion one line above (`:299`, published = what each package's `files[]` actually ships) and its measurement rule (`:301`, grep the `files[]` paths; zero hits means not published) override when the measurement contradicts it, and here it does, by the dev's own reading. AGENTS.md outranks os-dev.md on a conflict either way. Owed: one `.changeset/*.md` with `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, describing the docblock correction (packages suggest `everyone` only; no door binds `guest` until ADR-0138 D3 item 5's door is built), the `skip-changeset` label removed, and `Clause-②: no` kept in the PR body (no accept-set moves, so no ADR-0087 marker and no `minor`).
- `@objectstack/lint` (`18.0.0-next.2`, not private): the no-publish reading is right; nothing in its `files[]` changes.

- The Tier H word is not spent by the fix: the APPROVED review on this head carries later pushes (Prime Directive 14), so adding the changeset needs no second approval.
